claims.text: Post-casting annealing optimized around 800 °C for 15 minutes followed by rapid quenching will form nanoscale precipitates in AlCoCrFeNi2-like eutectic high-entropy alloys.
The annealing-induced precipitates will be uniformly distributed within the softer FCC phase.
The proposed treatment will increase yield strength by approximately 20% relative to the as-cast state.
The proposed treatment will maintain or improve ductility relative to the as-cast state.
Precise tuning of the annealing and quenching parameters can keep the precipitates in the nanoscale regime.
Annealing at approximately 800 °C for 15 minutes followed by rapid quenching avoids excessive precipitate coarsening.
The treatment forms uniformly dispersed nanoscale intermetallic precipitates within the ductile FCC phase.
The nanoscale precipitates refine phase interfaces.
The nanoscale precipitates impede dislocation motion.
Thermal activation during annealing promotes nucleation of nanoscale precipitates.
Obstruction of dislocation motion by the precipitates produces precipitation hardening.
The precipitate-modified microstructure improves ductility by enhancing stress redistribution across refined phase boundaries.
The annealed material will show improved elongation at fracture relative to the as-cast alloy.
Changes in annealing temperature, annealing time, or alloy composition may cause precipitate coarsening.
Precipitate coarsening may prevent simultaneous improvement of strength and ductility.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis allows ductility merely to be maintained, whereas the predicted outcome and falsification rule require improved or measurably enhanced ductility. An unchanged ductility result would therefore satisfy the main hypothesis but be classified as falsification.
